title: Community Heat Resilience Canvas
challenge: Neighborhood heat-response planning is fragmented across agencies and community organizations.
goal: Create a reviewable pilot that connects heat-risk evidence to neighborhood action.

constraints.statement: Data coverage and community capacity vary by neighborhood.

personas.name: Municipal Resilience Coordinator
personas.role: Coordinates heat preparedness across departments and partners.
personas.description: Needs a practical way to connect uneven evidence, community priorities, and operational decisions.
personas.context: Coordinates municipal departments, public-health teams, and neighborhood partners under time pressure.
jobs: Connect heat-risk evidence to a clear neighborhood action
Coordinate decisions across agencies and community partners
goals: Connect risk evidence to a clear neighborhood action
gains: A shared decision trail that all partners can review
Faster alignment without hiding evidence gaps
behaviors: Reviews multiple dashboards before convening partners
Uses printable briefs during cross-agency meetings
barriers: Different evidence standards across partner organizations
motivations: Protect residents while using public resources responsibly
Build durable trust with neighborhood partners
accessibility_needs: Plain-language summaries for mixed technical audiences
quotes: I need everyone to see the same evidence gap before we commit resources.

says: We need a decision everyone can explain and defend.
thinks: Which evidence gap could undermine this pilot later?
does: Compares dashboards, workshop notes, and operational constraints.
feels: Responsible for moving quickly without overstating certainty.
sees: Different teams using different definitions of priority.
hears: Community partners asking how decisions will affect their neighborhoods.
gains: A shared decision trail that all partners can review.

attributes.statement: Uses printable briefs during cross-agency meetings.
Values defensible decisions over rapid public claims.

personas.source_notes: Synthesized from workshop observations and the current pilot dataset.
personas.confidence_notes: Operational behaviors are better supported than motivational claims.

stakeholders.name: Neighborhood partner coalition
stakeholders.engagement_strategy: Review assumptions and neighborhood feasibility before pilot approval.
tensions: Community urgency may conflict with municipal procurement timelines
stakeholders.notes: Must review intervention assumptions before pilot launch.

journeys.title: Neighborhood heat-action planning journey
journeys.scenario: The resilience coordinator moves from detecting a neighborhood heat-risk signal to agreeing on an operational pilot with community partners.
journeys.desired_outcome: A shared, evidence-aware pilot decision with explicit ownership and review checkpoints.

stages.name: Detect
opportunities: Show confidence and missingness beside each signal

stages.name: Align
questions: Do we agree on the problem and constraints?
thoughts: Do we agree on the problem and constraints?
pain_points: Different organizations use different evidence standards
frictions: Different organizations use different evidence standards

stages.name: Commit
actions: Select a pilot action and accountable owner
questions: Can we test this without overstating impact?
thoughts: Can we test this without overstating impact?
pain_points: Pressure to communicate before evidence is complete
frictions: Pressure to communicate before evidence is complete
opportunities: Add explicit claims, assumptions, and review dates

behavioral_signals.interpretation: Printable briefs receive repeated use and may warrant further qualitative study.
behavioral_signals.limitation: Download activity indicates engagement but does not prove user intent, identity, motivation, or demographic attributes.

point_of_view.statement: Municipal Resilience Coordinator needs a practical way to address 'Neighborhood heat-response planning is fragmented across agencies and community organizations.' so they can create a reviewable pilot that connects heat-risk evidence to neighborhood action without ignoring the constraint: Data coverage and community capacity vary by neighborhood.

how_might_we.question: How might we help Municipal Resilience Coordinator make the challenge concrete enough to act on?
How might we turn the goal — Create a reviewable pilot that connects heat-risk evidence to neighborhood action — into a small testable experiment?
How might we make the constraint visible without letting it stop progress?
How might we document assumptions so the next decision can be reviewed?

framework.name: Jobs To Be Done
framework.description: Frame the progress a person is trying to make in a specific situation.
limitations: Can underrepresent institutional and collective dynamics

prompts.label: I want to
prompts.question: What progress is the user trying to make?
prompts.purpose: Describe the job without prescribing a solution.

prompts.label: Constraint
prompts.question: What prevents the user from making progress today?

custom_frameworks.name: Equity Lens
custom_frameworks.description: Review who benefits, who bears cost, and who participates in decisions.
limitations: Does not replace engagement with affected groups

prompts.label: Benefits
prompts.question: Who is expected to benefit, and what evidence supports that expectation?

prompt_packs.name: Heat pilot prompts
prompt_packs.description: Reusable prompts for neighborhood heat-response ideation.

prompts.label: Smallest test
prompts.question: What is the smallest neighborhood action that can produce useful learning?

ideas.title: Evidence-gap action card
ideas.description: Pair one heat signal with its confidence, missing data, proposed action, and review owner.
ideas.author: Program Design Team
ideas.rationale: Makes the key evidence limitation visible at the point of action.

ideas.title: Neighborhood confidence legend
ideas.description: Add a plain-language confidence and missingness legend to every neighborhood view.
ideas.author: Neighborhood partner coalition
ideas.rationale: Partners need a shared way to interpret uneven data quality.

ideas.title: Merged evidence note
ideas.description: Earlier wording folded into the action-card concept.
ideas.author: Municipal resilience coordinator
ideas.rationale: Preserve the originating concept and merge decision.

idea_clusters.name: Visible evidence gaps
idea_clusters.description: Concepts that keep missingness and confidence visible.
idea_clusters.rationale: Both concepts reduce false certainty during pilot selection.

ideation_summary.indicator_note: Ideation indicators describe recorded activity and lineage. Votes and selections represent participant judgment, not objective quality.

sources.title: Neighborhood heat indicators
sources.creator: Municipal analytics team
sources.description: Available heat, vulnerability, and service-access indicators with known coverage gaps.
sources.provenance_note: Registered from the pilot evidence inventory.

sources.title: Neighborhood partner planning interview
sources.creator: Program Design Team
sources.description: Interview about evidence gaps and implementation constraints.
sources.provenance_note: Consent and use restrictions must be reviewed before publication.

evidence.title: Neighborhood heat indicators
evidence.summary: Available heat, vulnerability, and service-access indicators with known coverage gaps.

evidence.title: Partner statement about shared evidence
evidence.summary: Partners need evidence gaps to remain visible during pilot selection.
evidence.quote: We need everyone to see the same evidence gap before we commit resources.

claims.statement: A shared one-page pilot brief can improve cross-agency decision clarity.
claims.uncertainty: No before-and-after comparison has been completed.
limitations: Evidence is based on a single interview and workshop observations.

claims.statement: The available indicators identify individual vulnerability.
limitations: Ecological data cannot establish individual conditions.
contradictions: The review note prohibits individual-level interpretation.

assumptions.statement: A shared one-page pilot brief will improve cross-agency decision clarity.
assumptions.consequence: If false, the format may add work without improving alignment.
assumptions.test_method: Compare reviewer interpretation before and after using the brief.

research_questions.question: Which evidence gaps most often block a shared pilot decision?

interview_guides.title: Cross-agency decision clarity interview
interview_guides.purpose: Understand where evidence and ownership become unclear.
questions: What would make the next action reviewable?

observation_notes.title: Pilot planning workshop
observation_notes.note: Participants used different definitions of neighborhood priority and asked for visible confidence notes.

ledger_summary.indicator_note: Coverage indicators describe recorded links and workflow gaps; they do not measure truth or research quality.

handoffs.purpose: Register the pilot dataset and interview record.
handoffs.context_note: Preserve Canvas challenge, claim, and limitation context.

prototypes.title: Neighborhood heat-action brief
prototypes.description: A printable brief linking one neighborhood risk signal to one operational response and one review checkpoint.

tests.title: Cross-agency clarity review
tests.signal: Reviewers independently identify the same next action and evidence gap.
tests.method: Run a 30-minute review with municipal and community partners.
tests.learning_goal: Determine whether the brief supports a shared pilot decision.

review_notes.note: Do not treat incomplete neighborhood indicators as proof of individual vulnerability.
